exam.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Commerce - Commercial Operations and Associated Risks
exam.instructions: Answer all questions. Show your working out clearly for calculation questions. Write structured and justified answers for evaluation and option questions. Total time allowed: 90 minutes.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following business activities is classified under the primary sector?
Which one of the following insurance principles requires the proposer to reveal all relevant material facts truthfully when completing a proposal form?

questions.correct_answer: A trade agreement between a group of countries for the removal or reduction of trade barriers between them.
An application form completed by an individual or business requesting insurance cover and detailing the risk to be covered.

questions.question_text: A shop in Malaysia sells a coffee for •8.00 euros. The exchange rate is •1.00 euro = 4.93 MYR. Calculate the price of the coffee in Malaysian Ringgit (MYR). Show your working.
Calculate, to 2 decimal places, the monthly payment for a bicycle priced at 1 399.00 South African Rand (ZAR) if paid across 12 equal monthly installments. Show your working.
Explain one benefit to a retail business of purchasing stock directly from a wholesaler rather than directly from manufacturers.
questions.correct_answer: Wholesalers break bulk (1), which enables small retailers to purchase smaller quantities of goods as needed (1), reducing the amount of storage space and cash tied up in inventory (1).

questions.question_text: Explain one reason why an insurance policy will include specific clauses.
questions.correct_answer: Clauses clarify the exact terms and limits of coverage to the customer (1), making it legal and explicit what conditions or events are excluded (1), thereby preventing fraudulent or invalid claims from being paid out (1).

questions.question_text: Categorize the following economic activities into their respective economic sectors.
questions.correct_answer: Primary Sector: Farming, Iron Ore Mining; Secondary Sector: Car Production; Tertiary Sector: Retailing

questions.question_text: Match the commercial trade term on the left with its correct definition on the right.
right_items: Financial support provided by a government to local producers
A tax imposed on imported goods
A physical limit on the quantity of goods that can be imported
A complete official prohibition on trade with a specific country
questions.correct_answer: Tariff: A tax imposed on imported goods; Quota: A physical limit on the quantity of goods that can be imported; Embargo: A complete official prohibition on trade with a specific country; Subsidy: Financial support provided by a government to local producers

questions.question_text: Fill in the missing words regarding commercial insurance concepts: Under the principle of [blank], the insured is placed back into the exact financial position held immediately prior to the loss. If an insurer pays full compensation for destroyed goods, the principle of [blank] gives the insurer legal ownership of any salvageable scrap. Additionally, a proposer must hold an [blank] in the subject matter to legally take out cover.
State whether the following statement is True or False: 'A hotel business can purchase standard commercial insurance cover against failing to make a profit due to normal economic competition.'
questions.correct_answer: False (Normal market loss or failure to make a profit is an uninsurable risk because actuaries cannot calculate the mathematical probability of non-profitability).

questions.question_text: Place the standard commercial documents in chronological order of use during a trade transaction.
questions.correct_answer: 1. Quotation, 2. Purchase Order, 3. Delivery Note, 4. Invoice

label_prompts: Document A: Issued by seller providing price estimate prior to ordering
Document B: Signed by buyer upon receipt of delivered goods
Document C: Issued by seller requesting payment for goods supplied
questions.correct_answer: Document A: Quotation; Document B: Delivery Note; Document C: Invoice

questions.question_text: Analyse the benefits for a retail clothing chain like Truworths of holding Public Liability Insurance.
questions.correct_answer: AO2: Public liability insurance protects Truworths against legal claims if a member of the public or tradesperson (such as an electrician) trips, falls, or is injured on store premises. AO3: By holding this cover, Truworths avoids potentially catastrophic financial losses from court compensation payouts or legal fees, ensuring business stability and encouraging third-party contractors to work on site securely.

questions.question_text:
Amazon is considering two options for locating an additional logistics warehouse in India:
Option 1: Locating near to major transport links (rail and highways).
Option 2: Locating at a large site with space to expand later.
Justify which one of these two options Amazon should choose.
questions.correct_answer:
Option 1 Arguments:
AO2: Locating near major transport links allows rapid dispatch of goods to urban areas and enables employees to commute easily by public transport.
AO3: Faster delivery improves customer satisfaction and repeat sales. However (AO4), road traffic congestion or higher land costs near transport hubs could raise operating expenses.
Option 2 Arguments:
AO2: A large site allows Amazon to store a vastly wider product range and accommodate future order volume growth.
AO3: Consolidating inventory in one expanding site saves the expense of opening multiple smaller hubs. However (AO4), if land is located far from city centers, long-distance delivery times will increase.
Conclusion: Option 1 is preferable for e-commerce where rapid delivery speed is the prime competitive advantage.

questions.question_text: Evaluate why a small independent pet shop like The Pet Safari can survive and remain profitable when competing directly against large pet supermarket chains. You should use your knowledge of commerce in your answer.
questions.correct_answer:
AO1: Small retailers survive by providing personalized customer service, specialized knowledge, and flexible purchase options.
AO2: The Pet Safari offers tailored nutrition advice for dogs/cats and sells fresh, custom-quantities of pet food, whereas large pet chains offer mostly standardized, pre-packaged goods.
AO3: Specialized customer service creates personal relationships and customer loyalty, encouraging word-of-mouth recommendations and repeat visits.
AO4: On the other hand, large pet stores benefit from purchasing economies of scale, allowing them to undercut prices and offer a broader range of general merchandise. Furthermore, small shops face higher overhead costs per unit.
Conclusion/Judgement: Despite price disadvantages, small independent retailers like The Pet Safari survive successfully by differentiating themselves through niche custom products and expert high-touch service that large automated competitors cannot replicate.
